articles.headline: US strike on an alleged drug boat kills 3 in the eastern Pacific Ocean
articles.summary: The latest attack brings the number of people who have been killed in boat strikes by the U.S. military to at least 211 since the Trump administration began targeting those it calls "narcoterrorists" in early September.
articles._summary: President Donald Trump speaks during a Cabinet meeting at the White House, Wednesday, May 27, 2026, in Washington, as Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, looks on. Jacquelyn Martin/AP hide caption WASHINGTON — The U.S. military attacked a boat accused of smuggling drugs in the eastern Pacific Ocean on Thursday, killing three people, as the Trump administration wages a monthslong campaign against alleged traffickers in Latin America. The latest attack brings the number of people who have been killed in boat strikes by the U.S. military to at least 211 since the Trump administration began targeting those it calls "narcoterrorists" in early September. As with most of the military's statements on strikes in the eastern Pacific Ocean and Caribbean Sea, U.S. Southern Command said it targeted the alleged drug traffickers along known smuggling routes. The military did not provide evidence that the vessel was ferrying drugs.

articles.headline: What Iran and US get from deal and why both could struggle to keep it
articles.summary: BBC analysts assess the claims by both Washington and Tehran to have won a victory with the deal to end their war.
articles._summary: More than 100 days after US and Israeli bombs began falling on Iran, both sides are claiming victory - a sign of how much each needed a way out. A deal has officially ended the fighting, but the harder negotiations are just beginning. Both sides have sold the deal to their public as a win but, as our analysts here explain, neither has fully convinced them and domestic critics on both sides argue that too many concessions were made. For Iran , the deal with the US offers something just as important as a ceasefire: a way to claim that it has not just survived the war without surrendering but has emerged from it stronger. From the start, Tehran's core objective was not necessarily to defeat the US and Israel in conventional military terms. It was to come out of the conflict with the Islamic Republic intact, its leadership still functioning and its negotiating position not completely broken.
articles._zh_headline: 伊朗和美国从协议中得到什么以及为什么双方都可能难以维持协议
articles._zh_summary: 美国和以色列向伊朗投下炸弹一百多天后，双方都宣称取得了胜利，这表明双方都多么需要出路。协议正式结束了战斗，但更艰难的谈判才刚刚开始。双方都将这笔交易视为一场胜利，但正如我们的分析师所解释的那样，双方都没有完全说服自己，双方的国内批评者都认为双方做出了太多让步。对于伊朗来说，与美国的协议提供了与停火同样重要的东西：一种方式来宣称它不仅在战争中幸存下来并且没有投降，而且在战争中变得更加强大。从一开始，德黑兰的核心目标不一定是在常规军事方面击败美国和以色列。它将完整地摆脱与伊斯兰共和国的冲突，其领导层仍在发挥作用，其谈判地位也没有完全被打破。

articles.headline: Bowen: US-Iran deal raises inescapable question of what the war was for
articles.summary: While the human cost is clear, the Iranian regime has not just survived the war, it has been empowered.
articles._summary: The memorandum of understanding signed by President Donald Trump and President Masoud Pezeshkian of Iran lays out the political, military and economic consequences of the ill-judged decision to attack Iran on 28 February. The human cost is already clear. Thousands have been killed, many of them civilians, in Iran and Lebanon. The US, and by extension Israel, have suffered a strategic defeat. The regime in Tehran faced its worst nightmare: a joint military operation to cripple or destroy it by the US, the world's strongest power, and Israel, the Middle East's superpower. The regime has not just survived. It has been empowered. Its strategy of blocking the Strait of Hormuz, and with it one fifth of the world's supplies of oil and gas as well as other vital components in the global economy, has forced Trump to agree to a series of concessions that have infuriated and alarmed America's Iran hawks and the Israeli government.

articles.headline: Student loan borrowers will get an interest rate cut if they sign up for auto pay
articles.summary: The Trump administration wants to jumpstart student loan repayment, with federal student loan debt approaching $2 trillion.
articles._summary: Student loan borrowers who enroll in automatic payments will get a much bigger discount on interest starting July 1, the U.S. Department of Education says. Auto pay has long offered a modest discount off borrowers' interest rate — .25 percentage points — but after millions of borrowers opted out during the long COVID repayment pause, with some making no payments for years , the nation's student debt portfolio swelled to $1.7 trillion. On Thursday, the department said it will temporarily increase its auto pay interest rate discount to one full percentage point. Practically, that means an undergraduate borrower with a loan at the current 6.39% would see their interest rate drop temporarily to 5.39%. The rate cut will last for two years, from July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2028. Borrowers already enrolled in auto pay do not need to act. They will automatically receive the rate cut.
